name: Tampa
metroName: Tampa-St. Petersburg-Clearwater, FL Metropolitan Statistical Area

electric.name: Tampa Electric (TECO)
electric.serves: About 870,000 customers across 2,000 square miles of Hillsborough County and parts of Pasco, Pinellas and Polk counties.

electric.name: Duke Energy Florida
electric.serves: About 2.0 million customers over roughly 20,000 square miles of west central Florida, including St. Petersburg and Clearwater (2026 Ten-Year Site Plan).

electric.name: Withlacoochee River Electric Cooperative (WREC)
electric.serves: Electric cooperative headquartered in Dade City (Pasco County). A customer testimonial on its homepage refers to WREC service in Pasco County. Its exact territory and programs were not researched.

gas.name: Peoples Gas
gas.serves: Statewide gas utility (500,000+ customers, an Emera company). Its site lists Tampa and St. Petersburg among its local areas (under 'Appliances and Sales'). Gas is available only at some addresses; check by ZIP code.

utilities.notes: The St. Petersburg/Clearwater side (Pinellas) is mostly Duke Energy Florida and Tampa/Hillsborough is TECO, but parts of Pinellas and Pasco are TECO too, so confirm by address. The brief's 'TECO Peoples Gas' now brands itself 'Peoples Gas'. Duke-run program pages on duke-energy.com blocked automated access, so Duke details come from Duke's newsroom and its PSC-filed 2026 Ten-Year Site Plan.

auditPrograms.name: Tampa Electric free in-home energy audit
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: A TECO energy analyst inspects the home, identifies savings, recommends TECO programs and gives year-round tips. TECO says team members hold AEE (ANSI-accredited) certification. The audit is also the gateway to TECO's ceiling insulation and duct repair programs, which require a pre-approval inspection.

auditPrograms.name: Tampa Electric Online Energy Audit (personalized or simple)
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: The personalized audit is for TECO customers who log in. The simple audit needs no account.
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: A report based on actual usage (personalized) or estimated usage from a home profile and weather (simple), with ways to cut energy costs.
auditPrograms.howToBook: Online from TECO's Energy Audit page.

auditPrograms.name: Duke Energy Florida Home Energy Check
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: All Duke Energy Florida residential customers, including renters and apartment residents, who have not had a Home Energy Check in the past two years.
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: An energy audit done online, by phone or in person (a walk-through), with personalized recommendations. Duke also provides a kit of easy-install energy-saving measures. Completing a check makes the customer eligible for Duke's home improvement rebates, which Duke describes as 'up to $3,800'.
auditPrograms.howToBook: Sign up through Duke Energy's Home Energy Check page on duke-energy.com, which is linked from Duke's June 24, 2026 news release. duke-energy.com blocked automated access, so the booking page itself was not read.
auditPrograms.status: open (promoted by Duke on 2026-06-24 and 2026-08-05; no end date published)

auditPrograms.name: Peoples Gas Online Energy Audit (personalized or simple)
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: The personalized audit is for Peoples Gas customers who log in. The simple audit needs no account.
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: The personalized audit gives a report based on your home's actual gas use, plus alerts. The simple audit estimates use from a home profile and local weather. Both point to natural gas appliance options.
auditPrograms.howToBook: Online at the Peoples Gas Energy Audit page. There is no appointment.

rebates.name: Tampa Electric Heating & Cooling rebate
rebates.amount: $40 for systems rated SEER 16.00 / SEER2 15.20 (geothermal EER 14.0+); $550 for SEER 17.00 / SEER2 16.20 (geothermal EER 15.0+). Paid per condensing unit and matched to the invoice if the system costs less than the rebate.
rebates.whoQualifies: All TECO residential customers replacing an old system with a new ducted heat pump, straight-cool/natural-gas-heat system (new furnace required; propane doesn't qualify) or geothermal system. Ductless mini-splits are not eligible. A contractor with a Tampa Electric vendor number deducts the rebate on the invoice, or homeowners can use the page's 'self-install option'. Apply within 90 days of installation.

rebates.name: Tampa Electric Ceiling Insulation rebate
rebates.amount: $0.16 per square foot per R-11 of insulation installed
rebates.whoQualifies: TECO residential customers. A pre-approval attic inspection by a TECO energy analyst is required (call 813-275-3909), and the rebate certificate is valid for one year. Owner-installed and participating-contractor work both qualify. Apply within 90 days.

rebates.name: Tampa Electric Ductwork (duct repair) program
rebates.amount: A TECO-approved contractor seals the duct leaks 'for only $125' per heating and cooling unit (customer price; extensive repairs cost extra).
rebates.whoQualifies: TECO residential customers. A pre-approval inspection of the duct system by a TECO energy analyst is required.

rebates.name: Tampa Electric ENERGY STAR smart thermostat rebate
rebates.whoQualifies: TECO customers buying a new ENERGY STAR smart thermostat. Apply within 90 days of purchase. Not compatible with TECO's Energy Planner rate.

rebates.name: Tampa Electric Prime Time Plus
rebates.amount: Automatic monthly bill credits that TECO says 'can add up to hundreds of dollars per year', plus a free ENERGY STAR smart thermostat
rebates.whoQualifies: TECO residential customers who enroll eligible HVAC, water heaters, pool pumps or Level 2 EV chargers for occasional power pauses. Minimum of 400 kWh/month delivered consumption to receive credits.

rebates.name: Duke Energy Florida home improvement rebates (Residential Incentive Program)
rebates.amount: 'Up to $3,800 in rebates' after a free Home Energy Check (Duke, June 24 and Aug. 5, 2026). Per-measure amounts were not verified because duke-energy.com blocked automated access.
rebates.whoQualifies: Duke Energy Florida residential customers who have completed a Home Energy Check. Measures named by Duke include attic insulation, HVAC, duct repair and energy-efficient windows. The 2026 Ten-Year Site Plan also lists home energy management systems.

rebates.name: Peoples Gas residential energy conservation rebates
rebates.runBy: Peoples Gas (Peoples Gas System, an Emera company)
rebates.amount: Replacing electric with natural gas / replacing gas with gas: tank water heater $550 / $350; ENERGY STAR tank water heater $650 / $400; tankless water heater $700 / $550; cooking $300 / $100; clothes drying $300 / $150; gas furnace $725 / $500; gas space conditioning $500 per ton / $150 per ton. The rebate cannot exceed the total cost of equipment, installation, piping and venting.
rebates.whoQualifies: Peoples Gas residential customers. Equipment must be installed within one year before applying. Used, refurbished or thrift-store appliances, propane conversions, point-of-use tankless units (minimum 5 gpm), fireplaces, fire pits, grills and portable heaters do not qualify. For electric-to-gas conversions the invoice must say 'electric to gas'. CLEAResult may verify the installation by smartphone.
rebates.status: open (no end date published; Peoples Gas may change or end it without notice)

rebates.name: Tampa Electric Neighborhood Weatherization
rebates.amount: Free installed items (six LED bulbs, water heater pipe wrap, low-flow showerheads and aerators, weatherstripping, caulking and more) plus a free energy audit. Participants may also qualify for free duct sealing and ceiling insulation.
rebates.whoQualifies: TECO customers living in one of the communities TECO has identified. Call 813-275-3909 to check. TECO refers others to YOU THRIVE's Weatherization Assistance Program.

stateHomeEnergyRebates.programName: Florida Energy Saver Program: HOMES (Home Owner Managing Energy Savings) and HEEHR (High-Efficiency Electric Home Rebates, Florida's name for HEAR)
stateHomeEnergyRebates.administrator: Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS), Office of Energy
stateHomeEnergyRebates.summary: The state portal says both programs 'are expected to launch in the future' and that 'additional information on the program timeline will be made available soon'. Homeowners can only register and fill in a profile to be emailed when applications open. Florida has about $346 million in federal funding. Planned HEEHR caps: heat pump $8,000; heat pump water heater $1,750; electric stove/cooktop/range/oven or heat pump dryer $840; panel (load service center) $4,000; insulation, air sealing and ventilation $1,600; wiring $2,500; up to $14,000 per household. It covers 100% of project cost under 80% of area median income (AMI) and 50% at 80-150% AMI. Households over 150% AMI are not eligible. Planned single-family HOMES limits (20-34% modeled savings / 35%+): under 80% AMI $16,000 / $20,000 (up to 100% of cost); 80% AMI and above $2,000 / $4,000 (up to 50% of cost). These pages carry a 2025 copyright and predate DOE's May 2026 program notices, so final terms (for example fuel switching under HEEHR) may change. On June 8, 2026 U.S. Rep. Kathy Castor said Florida's funding was approved in January 2025 but has been delayed since.

incomeQualified.name: Weatherization Assistance Program: Hillsborough, Pasco and Hernando counties
incomeQualified.runBy: You Thrive Florida (YOU THRIVE), the FloridaCommerce-listed local provider
incomeQualified.summary: For low-income homeowners with gross household income no more than 200% of federal poverty guidelines. Priority goes to people 60+, people with disabilities, families with children under 18 and high-energy-burden households. An audit decides the measures: air sealing, attic insulation, duct sealing, and HVAC or refrigerator replacement if testing warrants. It is 'not a window replacement program'. Apply online with full documentation; incomplete applications are denied. Funding-dependent. Phone (FloridaCommerce list): (352) 796-1427.

incomeQualified.name: Weatherization Assistance Program: Pinellas County
incomeQualified.summary: Local WAP provider for Pinellas: (727) 327-0977. FloridaCommerce says WAP applications are available only from the local provider.

incomeQualified.name: Tampa Electric Neighborhood Weatherization
incomeQualified.summary: Free energy-saving items plus a free audit, and possibly free duct sealing and ceiling insulation, for TECO customers in TECO-identified qualifying communities. TECO says it has served more than 40,000 customers.

incomeQualified.name: Duke Energy Florida Neighborhood Energy Saver
incomeQualified.summary: Free energy-saving measures for low-income customers in neighborhoods that meet income criteria. Measures include air infiltration, water heating, lighting, insulation, duct repair, and heat pump/AC tune-ups, plus smart thermostats. Duke plans about 5,775 homes a year (2026 Ten-Year Site Plan). Duke picks the neighborhoods, so there is no individual application.

incomeQualified.name: Duke Energy Florida Low Income Weatherization Assistance Program
incomeQualified.runBy: Duke Energy Florida with local agencies
incomeQualified.summary: Duke funds weatherization and efficiency measures for low-income customers through local agency partners, about 500 customers a year (2026 Ten-Year Site Plan).

incomeQualified.name: Florida Energy Saver Program HEEHR (when launched)
incomeQualified.summary: Planned rebates of up to $14,000 for households under 150% AMI. Not launched as of 2026-10-12.

localRules.name: No local building benchmarking or performance standard found (Tampa, St. Petersburg, Clearwater)
localRules.appliesTo: Not applicable. No local mandate affects homeowners or large buildings.
localRules.summary: IMT's January 2026 national comparison of commercial building benchmarking policies lists no jurisdiction in the Tampa metro. City ordinances were not individually checked.

localRules.name: Florida Building Energy-Efficiency Rating Act: disclosure at sale (s. 553.996, Florida Statutes)
localRules.appliesTo: Every sale of real property with a building on it, including ordinary single-family homes. It affects homeowners who sell or buy.
localRules.summary: Before or when the buyer signs the contract, they must be given information telling them they can get an energy-efficiency rating on the building. The information covers how to analyze the rating, comparisons to statewide averages, ways to improve the rating, and a notice that a rating may qualify the buyer for an energy-efficient mortgage. This is a disclosure of information only. No rating or audit is required.

localRules.name: State preemption of local energy-source and appliance restrictions (s. 366.032, Florida Statutes)
localRules.appliesTo: Applies statewide and limits local governments. It affects homeowners indirectly.
localRules.summary: Counties, cities and other local bodies may not restrict or prohibit the types or fuel sources of energy that utilities and gas suppliers deliver, or appliances (including stoves and grills) that use them. The only exception is enforcing the Florida Building Code or Fire Prevention Code. In practice no Florida city or county can adopt a gas ban or all-electric mandate for homes.

notes: MSA: CBSA 45300 (OMB July 2023): Hernando, Hillsborough, Pasco and Pinellas counties. TECO's heating and cooling rebate has two very different levels: $40 at SEER2 15.20 versus $550 at SEER2 16.20. Ductless mini-splits get nothing. TECO moved to its PSC-approved 2025-2034 DSM plan on June 1, 2025 (Consummating Order PSC-2025-0137-CO-EG, docket 20240163-EG). Its 2026 Ten-Year Site Plan lists four residential audit types, ceiling insulation, duct repair, ENERGY STAR thermostats, heating and cooling, Neighborhood Weatherization, Prime Time Plus and Energy Planner. Duke Energy Florida's per-measure rebate amounts could not be read (duke-energy.com blocked automated access). Only Duke's 'up to $3,800' total after a Home Energy Check is verified. The research tool's web-search budget ran out partway through, so some leads (WREC programs, city-level ordinances) were not followed up. Federal tax credits: the IRS says the Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit (25C) can be claimed for improvements made through December 31, 2025, and the Residential Clean Energy Credit (25D) 'is not available for any property placed in service after December 31, 2025.' Do not list either as a current incentive. Federal rule change for the IRA rebates: DOE Program Notices 26-1 (HOMES) and 26-2 (HEAR/HEEHR), effective May 29, 2026, removed fuel-switching (gas/propane-to-electric) from HEAR so it now covers only electric-to-electric upgrades, and generally require insulation/air sealing to be addressed before heating and cooling upgrades. Launched states had to comply within three months; per NASEO's August 2026 FAQ, reservations made on or after September 1, 2026 must follow the new notices and DOE is extending award periods to September 30, 2031.
